ai.description: The Medo Pit Viper reaches 60–70 cm. It is green with a reddish-brown tail and a distinct postocular stripe. It features a triangular head and a prominent white ventrolateral line.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Trimeresurus medoensis* is best distinguished by its distinct, narrow reddish-brown or dark post-ocular stripe that extends onto the neck, unlike the broader patterns of similar species.
ai.habitat: The Medo pit viper inhabits dense subtropical evergreen forests and montane broadleaf woodlands, typically found at elevations ranging from 1,000 to 2,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Medo pit viper is primarily nocturnal, often positioning itself on low-hanging branches or near streams to ambush unsuspecting prey under the cover of darkness.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Trimeresurus medoensis* is ovoviviparous, giving birth to live young. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, with females producing small litters of 3–8 offspring.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Medo Pit Viper is found in Northeast India, specifically in Arunachal Pradesh, inhabiting high-elevation forests in the Eastern Himalayas.
